LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. Green Bay is set as a 3.5-point favorite at home in this primetime matchup, and it’s looking to stay over .500 in the 2026 season after a Week 7 loss to Detroit. Despite a three-game winning streak earlier this season and a 4-3 record overall, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North heading into Week 8. So, every game means a ton for Jordan Love, Matt LaFleur and Co. as they look to get back to the playoffs. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. Still, oddsmakers aren’t expecting them to have another blowout loss with this spread set inside a touchdown on Thursday. All week long, the SI Betting team has shared our favorite game picks, props, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more for Panthers vs. Packers. Here’s a quick look at some of our favorites to give our readers a one-stop shop to prepare for Thursday Night Football. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. I'll take the Packers to cover on Thursday Night Football. Packers running back Josh Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but he returned in Week 7 and made an immediate impact against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs played just 52.2 percent of Green Bay’s offense snaps, but he saw 18 opportunities (11 rushes, seven targets) and ended up finding the end zone. The former first-round pick had 11 carries for 36 yards and caught five of his seven targets for 55 yards (and a receiving score) in the loss to Detroit. He has a great matchup against a Carolina defense that is 30th in EPA/Rush, 32nd in yards per carry allowed and 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed (11) this season. While this isn’t the most favorable price, Jacobs has been a touchdown machine in his Packers career, scoring 31 times in 33 games. He’s an easy bet against one of the worst run defenses in the NFL. Bryce Young has been one of the best passers in the NFL even with his rough showing in Week 7 against Tampa Bay. In six games, Young has thrown for 1,712 yards and 12 scores, reaching at least 281 passing yards in five of his six games. He’s also posted four games with multiple touchdown passes. Green Bay is fifth in the NFL in EPA/Pass, but the Lions showed in Week 7 that you can throw on this team by attacking the outside corners. They lined Amon-Ra St. Brown – usually their slot receiver – outside quite a bit, and he finished the day 153 receiving yards. Plus, deep-ball threat Jameson Williams had two scores and 91 yards in the win. So, I expect Young and the Panthers to air it out against Green Bay, which has still allowed nine passing scores this season. Young has 36 or more pass attempts in five of his six games, so I think he’s a strong bounce-back candidate after a weird Week 7 game got out of hand very quickly for Carolina. Love has thrown the ball quite a bit in the 2026 season, and former first-round pick Matthew Golden has been one of the biggest beneficiaries. Through seven games, Golden has 69 targets, 36 catches and 540 receiving yards. He’s also found the end zone three times. Now, Love and Golden haven’t connected as much as you’d expect given his target share, but the second-year wideout still has five games with at least five receptions. Golden also has six or more targets in every game and four games with 12 or more looks. So, the volume should be there against a Carolina defense that is pretty average against the pass (13th in EPA/Pass) this season. I think Golden is undervalued at this number in Week 8. picks.blurb: Predictions: Will Packers Score Thursday Night Bounce-Back vs. Panthers? It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Here are the 10 most important Packers for tonight's game, a story filled with quotes and other good stuff by @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/tX2pc7MrfW Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Panthers Prediction I don't think this game is going to be pretty. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. Green Bay fell to 4-3 with a loss to Detroit in Week 7, and it's in last place in a loaded NFC North through seven weeks. Meanwhile, the Panthers (3-3) are in first place in the NFC South despite a major blowout loss at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Carolina made the playoffs in the 2025 season, but it has a ton of injuries on both sides of the ball that make it a tough team to trust against other quality opponents -- like Green Bay. Oddsmakers agree with that sentiment, as they've set the Packers as favorites at home to open this week. Panthers vs. Packers Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Panthers +3.5 (-110) Packers -3.5 (-110) Panthers: +154 Packers: -185 48.5 (Over -105/Under -115) There hasn't been a ton of movement in the odds for this game , as the Packers remain 3.5-point favorites at home. The total has jumped up from 47.5 to 48.5 while the moneyline has actually moved in Carolina's favor. According to DraftKings, just 22 percent of the moneyline bets and 41 percent of the spread bets are on the Panthers after their Week 7 showing against Tampa Bay. Earlier this week, I shared in SI Betting's preview for this game why I believe Green Bay is a worthwhile bet: The Panthers’ run defense was torched in Week 7 by Tampa Bay, and this could be a “get-right” spot for Matt LaFleur’s offense. Love should be able to attack through the air, as the Panthers are a below-average defense overall (20th in EPA/Play), and they entered Week 7 allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Meanwhile, Green Bay’s defense held a vaunted Detroit offense to just 20 points and is now fifth in the league in EPA/Play. If it weren’t for multiple missed field goals, the Pack could be entering this game with a 5-2 record. Carolina beat Detroit this season, but it has some confounding losses against Cleveland and at home against Tampa Bay. I don’t love this team – which is extremely banged up after Taylor Moton went down in Week 7 – on a short week against a Packers squad that has an above-average defense. I’m going to lay the points with a Green Bay team that needs this game a lot more than Carolina does if it’s going to make the playoffs. I'm not the only member of the SI Betting team taking Green Bay, as Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every NFL game, every week -- why he likes the Pack at home as well: I wrote about how I was out on the Panthers last week, and I proved to be right as they ended up on the wrong side of a blowout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. away.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. Hubbard doesn't have top-level breakaway speed, but he's tough and normally does the little things right and finds way

away.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle). Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

away.headline: Breaking down Packers' final injury report of Week 8 vs. Panthers
away.blurb: WR Matthew Golden (foot/shoulder): He returned in a limited capacity during Wednesday's walkthrough, keeping the door open to playing Thursday night. Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturidvant would be up next for snaps next to Christian Watson if Golden can't go. DL Devonte Wyatt (ankle): He hurt his ankle but returned to the game last week in Detroit. Cut he gut it out on a short week? The Packers will be thin at defensive tackle once again if Wyatt can't go. He needs to get healthy and start disrupting more plays. Edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr. (quad): He was a late add to the injury report this week, but he was able to get in a limited practice on Wednesday. away.headline: Panthers' concerns going into Thursday's game against the Packers just got even worse based on the final Week 8 injury report
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers had a lot of concerns going into this week after the beatdown the team suffered on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. To make things even harder, the Panthers had a short turnaround to make adjustments with a road trip coming up on Thursday against the Green Bay Packers. That already was going to be a rough road matchup for this team with everything going on coming out of the last game, and to make things even worse, the team's final Week 8 injury report added even more concerns. First off, the Panthers have officially ruled out star pass rusher Jaelan Phillips for the second consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Given the nature of the injury, the fact it's a reaggravation, and this being a short week, it was always unlikely that Phillips would have been able to play against the Packers. Wednesday's injury report confirmed those suspicions, leaving the Panthers without their top edge rusher. Being without Phillips really hurt the Panthers last week. Tampa Bay exposed the Panthers in the run game attacking the edges with counters and rumbled for over 250 yards on the ground. It was an embarrassing performance and not having Phillips out there to set the edge was a big reason for it, along with poor tackling. Big picture, sitting Phillips is the right call for him. He needs to get that hamstring figured out before rushing back into action like he did in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which is what caused this injury to reaggravate in the first place. The Panthers need Phillips for the long haul and need him fully healthy before returning. Another notable injury designation is left guard Damien Lewis, who will be out for Thursday's game due to a knee injury. Lewis was easily the team's best offensive lineman, allowing seven pressures this season on over 200 pass blocking snaps. The other four starters have each allowed 15+ pressures this season. The Panthers are also without backup guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and elevated Jake Curhan from the practice squad as a result. The Panthers also placed veteran right tackle Taylor Moton on the injured reserve earlier this week after he fractured his fibula along with further damage to his ankle. That leaves Monroe Freeling to fill back in at right tackle, which in turn forces Rasheed Walker to remain at left tackle. Those two have allowed a combined five sacks and 42 pressures. In Lewis place at left guard, the Panthers will likely turn to Corey Bullock, who's played 71 pass blocking snaps this season with one sack and five pressures allowed. It's a tough look for quarterback Bryce Young, who has been having to overcome pressure all season long. One more worrisome injury to note is in the secondary. Akayleb Evans will not play either due to a triceps/knee injury. Evans has been filling in as a starter, and largely has struggled, in place of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. home.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET. Both of these teams are considered Super Bowl contenders in the latest odds at the best betting sites , and they feature two of the best quarterbacks in the league. Lamar Jackson (ankle) has not played since the first half of Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, but he is expected to return on Sunday in what has suddenly become a huge game for the Ravens. Baltimore is 4-3 this season after going 1-2 in the games Jackson missed, and it’s in last place in the AFC North with every team in the division over .500. The Ravens dropped back-to-back key division games against Cleveland and Cincinnati without the two-time league MVP. Josh Allen – the MVP favorite this season – and the Bills are coming out of their bye week to play in this game, and they’re favored at home after a 5-1 start. Buffalo is looking to get the top spot in the AFC, and it benefitted from a Kansas City Chiefs loss (now 5-1 as well) during Week 7. Sunday’s game is the eighth meeting between Jackson and Allen all-time, with the Ravens holding a 3-2 edge in the regular season while Allen has won both of his playoff matchups against Jackson. Who has the edge in this regular-season clash? All season long, the SI Betting team has been predicting the final score of NFL games, and this one is no different. Using the latest odds and analysis from our team, here’s my score prediction for Sunday’s marquee matchup in Week 8. He certainly gives the Ravens’ offense a higher ceiling than backup Tyler Huntley. Unfortunately, I place my bets early in the week, so I don't have the benefit of knowing whether or not the two-time MVP will be on the field on Sunday. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. Buffalo’s defense is last in the NFL in EPA/Play and 30th in success rate, so this could be a get-right game for Jackson and Co. if he’s able to play at his full capabilities. It’s hard to put too much stock into the Ravens last three games without him, though their defense is now 13th in yards per play allowed and 15th in success rate. That’s not terrible, especially since Joe Burrow torched this team in the second half. I expect a high-scoring affair on Sunday, and it wouldn’t shock me if this came down to a final field goal. away.headline: Ravens' Lamar Jackson expected to miss rest of season with thumb injury: report
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is likely to miss the rest of the season after suffering a thumb injury Sunday on his first play since returning from a high ankle sprain, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport . Jackson missed Baltimore’s final three games in October due to his ankle issue before returning to action for the Ravens’ Week 8 road game against the Buffalo Bills. His comeback was short-lived, however, as the two-time MVP hurt his right thumb early in the first quarter of Sunday’s loss after hitting his hand on Bills linebacker Greg Rousseau’s arm on his follow-through on a pass attempt. Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter announced following the contest that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve (IR). To make matters worse, Ravens backup signal-caller Tyler Huntley also suffered an injury versus Buffalo, going down with a toe ailment in the first half. Baltimore’s emergency quarterback, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, took over and is currently in line to start the Ravens’ “Thursday Night Football” game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. Fagnano finished his NFL debut versus the Bills 10-for-21 with 91 passing yards, no touchdowns and one interception. Jackson has struggled to stay healthy in recent seasons, missing five games apiece during the 2021 and 2022 campaigns and four more contests last season. Baltimore started the year 4-1 and was at the top of the AFC North standings entering Week 6. The Ravens have lost three in a row since then, however, and are now in last place in the division at 4-4. away.headline: Cousins, Flacco, Daniel Jones Trades Pitched by NFL Insider After Lamar Jackson's Injury for Ravens
away.blurb: Sando's colleague Michael Silver threw out the idea of a reunion with Joe Flacco or acquiring the Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones or Chicago Bears' Tyson Bagent. Bleacher Report • 6h Aiyuk Hires New Agent to Help Return Two notable NFL insiders don't believe the Baltimore Ravens can sit idly by with franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson set to miss multiple weeks. Following Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills, coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson is headed for injured reserve due to a thumb injury. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley was also hurt in the defeat, forcing the team to turn to third-stringer Joe Fagnano. The Athletic's Mike Sando asserted the Ravens "need to find a quarterback, unless they're willing to pack it in." Lamar 'Balked' at Ravens Deal Predictions for Top Trade Candidates 🔮 He cast doubt on one potential option, questioning whether the Las Vegas Raiders would entertain a Kirk Cousins trade after the offseason saga surrounding Maxx Crosby. Sando also argued Cousins' solid production (2,124 yards, 19 touchdowns and five interceptions) may not be indicative of how he'd fare elsewhere. He had already played under Raiders coach Klint Kubiak before he signed with Las Vegas. ▶️ Full Ravens-Bills Recap 05:40 The Colts continue to sink further after having already traded away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Maybe they'd be willing to unload Jones' contract and start over at quarterback. Chicago can afford to deal Bagent when it also has Case Keenum on the roster. Keenum is arguably a better backup anyway. Bagent was coached by Baltimore offensive coordinator Declan Doyle last year, which is a factor to consider. Like Cousins, Flacco could be a nonstarter. The Cincinnati Bengals will need a lot of convincing to send him to a division rival with playoff aspirations. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Huntley "suffered what is thought to be a turf toe injury." Assuming he, like Jackson, will miss multiple games, Baltimore can't afford to move forward with Fagnano. The undrafted free agent went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against Buffalo. The fact that Bagent and Flacco are being floated as solutions illustrates the Ravens' bind, though. There aren't a lot of great QB options on the trade market right now and certainly not one who inspires a ton of confidence to lead a playoff push in the second half. 06:17 ▶️ Minshew Saves the Day TOP NEWS Colts Sticking With Daniel Jones Bleacher Report • 5h Russ' Emotional Reaction 🥲 Bleacher Report • 3h Jordan's Text to WNBA Finals MVP 🫡 Bleacher Report • 14h Ranking Best Fan Traditions 🙌 Bleacher Report • 7h New NFL Power Rankings 📊 Bleacher Report • 3h WWE Raw Live Grades 🔠 Bleacher Report • 9h Buzz: 2 Teams Eyeing RB Trade Bleacher Report • 8h Belichick won't confirm Jordon Hudson breakup Bleacher Report • 9h Eagles Vets May Be Traded

away.headline: Ravens report card, week 8: Another injury-riddled offensive implosion
away.blurb: Lamar Jackson’s injury on his first play of the game took the wind out of the team’s sails immediately. Tyler Huntley’s short stint in the opening quarter, prior to exiting with a foot injury, was eventful for the wrong reasons. Huntley’s four pass attempts resulted in zero yards and he lost a fumble in the Ravens’ own territory. Joe Fagnano made his NFL debut and played most of the game. After completing back-to-back throws immediately upon entering the game, Fagnano struggled. He completed 10-of-21 passes for only 93 yards with an interception and lost fumble. Fagnano also was banged up but finished the game. All three quarterbacks were under duress during their time on the field. The Ravens did an okay job bottling up the Bills’ run defense for most of the game. While they wound up with 146 rushing yards, James Cook was limited to 3.8 yards per carry with a longest run of 16 yards and Josh Allen ran seven times for 30 yards. Broderick Washington made a huge defensive play by coming up with an interception off a dropped pass, which led to the Ravens’ only touchdown of the game. Nnamdi Madubuike was the only defensive lineman to record a sack or quarterback hit. The Ravens’ cornerbacks were much better than last week, which was anticipated given they weren’t matching up with Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins again. Marlon Humphrey was beaten by D.J. Moore for a long 49-yard reception, but he was in position to make a play. He made a pass breakup on the very next play in the red zone and also nearly had an interception. Chidobe Awuzie had a nice pass defended as well in coverage of Kincaid and backup T.J. Tampa made an impact and his return to action. Tampa recovered a fumble and broke up a two-point conversion attempt. For the Ravens to be most successful in the backend, they might need to play Humphrey in the slot with Awuzie and Tampa taking outside corner reps opposite Wiggins. Keyon Martin, and Chandler Rivers when he was playing, often appear too undersized and overmatched. Rasheen Ali had a great kick return for 59 yards, where he appeared bottled up but then broke free for a huge gain. LaJohntay Wester had another quiet outing as a punt returner with just one return for two yards. Ryan Eckley also made some nice punts again, including a long 62-yarder. The biggest negative on special teams was another missed field goal from Tyler Loop, which came from just 34 yards out. In the grand scheme of a 26-point loss, one missed field goal is not a huge deal, but at the time it could have cut the Ravens’ deficit to three points. The Baltimore Ravens suffered a third consecutive loss in Week 8 and their second straight game losing by 20+ points, falling to the Buffalo Bills by a score of 36-10. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. John Lanfranca Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:01 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) will host the Tennessee Titans (1-6) in Week 8 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Bengals are 13.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the total set at over/under 45.5 points. Cincinnati is a -950 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is a +640 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Bengals predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 1. Titans vs Bengals pick: Bengals -13.5 (-110) My Bengals vs. Titans best bet is Cincinnati to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Titans vs Bengals NFL Odds Titans vs Bengals spread : Titans +13.5 (-110), Titans -13.5 (-110) Titans vs Bengals total : over/under 45.5 (-118o / 104u) Titans vs Bengals moneyline : Titans +640, Bengals -950 Titans vs Bengals Preview for NFL Week 8 Tennessee Titans Preview: Life Without Jeffery Simmons Fading the Titans has been a profitable endeavor this year, but they have covered the number in each of their last two road games. I provided the breakdown for their victory on the road in Indianapolis and their road cover as 11-point underdogs in Baltimore back in Week 4. I will not be going back to the well for a third time in this spot against the Bengals as too many factors are working against them. For starters, the Titans traded away their best defensive player this week in Jeffery Simmons and will also be without leading receiver in Carnell Tate. Opposing running backs have averaged four yards per carry against Tennessee with Simmons on the field — that number increases to 4.5 yards per carry on the 35 carries he has not been in the lineup. The Titans' explosive rush rate allowed also increases from 9.8% with Simmons to 14.3% without Simmons on the field. Simmons boasts the fifth-highest pass rush grade this season out of all defensive tackles , per Pro Football Focus. The lack of interior pressure will allow Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to build upon his red-hot finish to Week 7. Burrow was surgical in the second half versus Baltimore, completing 88% of his passes for an average of 13.8 yards per attempt. Burrow is heating up, as he historically does as the season progresses — and now, he gets a highly exploitable matchup. Tennessee's defense under head coach Robert Saleh ranks 31st in completion percentage allowed and 27th in yards per attempt allowed. The Titans' pressure rate of 30.6% ranks 26th. However, it is even more concerning when looking at the time charted to get those pressures on quarterbacks. The Titans' 2.8 seconds per pressure is the worst in the NFL, and that number is almost certainly going to get worse with the loss of Simmons. If Tennessee is going to make this game competitive, it has to be the doing of Cam Ward. Tony Pollard and the running game were excellent a week ago versus Cleveland, but the Bengals have the most improved run defense in the league. Cincinnati Bengals Preview: Good Spot for Cincy's Defense Al Golden's defense plays with the highest rate of light boxes in alignment, yet still leads the NFL in stuff rate defending running games. Golden can opt to add an extra defender on early downs to stymie Pollard, which will force Ward into long down-and-distance situations. Without their top weapon on the outside in Tate, the Titans lack playmakers to move the chains when they get to third down. Ward and company already struggle in these situations, ranking 27th in third-down conversion rate. The Bengals boast the eighth-best defense per dropback, according to expected points added (EPA). Projecting the Titans' success in this spot becomes extremely difficult when you consider that 43% of all their pass attempts on 2nd-and-8+ and 28% of all attempts on 3rd- or 4th-and-8+ longer were funneled to Tate. The Titans' passing game is facing an uphill battle in overcoming their deficiencies when their running game on standard downs isn't keeping them ahead of schedule. Titans vs Bengals Picks, Betting Analysis Tennessee has a -62 scoring margin in the first half of games this season, which is the worst in the league. The Titans will likely fall behind early and have no choice but to abandon the running game. This further puts the onus of any potential comeback in the hands of Cam Ward. Ward's 27.1 passer rating under pressure and turnover-worthy throw rate nearly doubling his big-time throw rate makes it too difficult to trust him in delivering any chance at a backdoor cover. The Bengals are -6.5 in the 1st half, which is another position worth a look. However, I am more comfortable allowing the full 60 minutes to play out as Ward's game-altering mistake(s) can come at any time. Joe Burrow is heating up at the right time and the Titans do not have the personnel to slow him down. I expect the Bengals to cruise to victory with significant margin. away.headline: Tennessee Titans’ 2027 NFL draft picks: Updated list after Jeffery Simmons trade
away.blurb: We are less than two weeks away from the NFL trade deadline, and there has already been a blockbuster deal. On Thursday morning, the Tennessee Titans dealt star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for a massive haul of draft picks. While the Bears land one of the best interior defensive linemen in the league, the Titans receive two first-round picks, a 2027 fourth-round pick, and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The trade is a major win for both sides, with the Bears now becoming a solid Super Bowl contender this year and beyond, while the Titans have some key building blocks for the future. With two loaded draft picks coming up, the Titans will be well-positioned to add young talent to their roster as they enter a full rebuild. An updated look at the Titans’ draft arsenal for the upcoming draft can be seen below. away.headline: Bengals rookie DE Cashius Howell injured vs Titans in NFL Week 8
away.blurb: Howell went to the locker room with trainers during the third quarter. The Bengals declared him out during the fourth quarter. Cincinnati Bengals rookie defensive end Cashius Howell injured his right wrist during the third quarter of the team's NFL Week 8 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium. Does Bengals head coach Zac Taylor expect Howell to be placed on injured reserve? Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. "We'll see," Taylor said Nov. 2 . "I'm not gonna say that yet, but probably trending in that direction." Taylor added that Howell had surgery on the wrist and will not play in the Bengals' Week 9 game against the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain. Howell joined fellow defensive linemen Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence II for a " three-man Sexy Dexy " after Lawrence's fourth-quarter sack against Baltimore. Howell was the Bengals' second-round pick (41st overall) in the 2026 NFL Draft , from Texas A&M . The 6-foot-2, 253-pound Howell was the first player selected by the Bengals in the 2026 draft. Defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence was acquired in a trade with the Giants for the 10th pick of the first round. Howell, who played two seasons for the Aggies after spending his first three college seasons at Bowling Green, was a Texas A&M teammate of Shemar Stewart , who wore No. 97 as a rookie before giving it to Lawrence . This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Bengals rookie DE Cashius Howell injured vs Titans in NFL Week 8

home.headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor updates the injury statuses of Cashius Howell, DJ Turner II and Cedric Johnson
home.blurb: But there is good injury news for the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) and defensive end Cedric Johnson (ankle) are day-to-day, and Taylor said he expects Turner to travel to Spain with the team when they fly out on Tuesday. All three players were ruled out of the game vs. the Titans early in the fourth quarter with their respective injuries. But the fact that Turner in particular is a true day-to-day per Taylor is good news against a Falcons receiving corps led by Drake London, who is sixth in the NFL in receiving yards (624). CINCINNATI, Ohio — When the Bengals travel to Madrid to face the Falcons this coming Sunday, they will be without one of their young pass rushers. Zac Taylor confirmed to reporters that rookie defensive end Cashius Howell had wrist surgery on Sunday night, hours after the Bengals’ 43-36 overtime win against the Titans . He didn’t confirm that Howell will go on injured reserve but that he is “probably trending in that direction.” Howell’s injury means more opportunities for his fellow former Texas A&M defensive end Shemar Stewart, who played against the Titans after being a healthy scratch a week prior against the Ravens. “Shemar has just been doing everything he can to control his spot, and we trust him to go in there to make some plays for us,” Taylor said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. home.headline: Ja’Marr Chase’s absence from Bengals practice gets an explanation in latest injury report
home.blurb: Chase (ankle) officially had a rest day, but is also listed with an ankle injury. He was seen in the locker room after practice. The “rest” being listed as the primary reason for his DNP insinuates it is not a serious injury, but seeing what the rest of his week looks like will be key before Sunday's game. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during last Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens and is back to being “week-to-week.” Coach Zac Taylor has already declared Dugger out for this week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen got his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle was limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) was also limited. Four Titans did not practice due to injuries including their first-round pick, WR Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate has played in all seven games for Tennessee this season, catching 34 passes for 413 yards and a touchdown. Fellow receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) went limited. He's been dealing with his hip injury for the last week and missed last Sunday's game because of it. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) was also a DNP. He's been playing next to All-Pro Jeffery Simmons and has produced 13 pressures and 1.5 sacks in seven games. Backup running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) were also non-participants Wednesday in Nashville. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. While nobody views the Cardinals as world-beaters, Arizona has looked like that against the Cowboys over the years after winning eight of the last nine meetings between these two teams. During the week, CeeDee Lamb even admitted it was "crazy" to know he has never beaten Arizona during his NFL career, which started in 2020. "Yeah, it's just crazy," Lamb said, per the team website. My Cardinals vs. Cowboys prediction favors Dallas riding the momentum of its Monday night win, with the Cowboys laying 6.5 points at home against Arizona today. A short week isn't typically a good thing, but after snapping a two-game skid, Dallas is chomping at the bit to get back on the field, especially with its explosive offense coming back to life. Here are my best NFL picks for Sunday, Nov. 1, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET from AT&T Stadium in Arlington. TOP PICK Cardinals vs Cowboys prediction: Cowboys -6.5 The Dallas Cowboys broke out of a two-game funk in which the offense stalled out on third downs. Against the Eagles, the Cowboys finished 9-for-14 on third/fourth downs and reclaimed their spot among the Top 5 attacks in Week 7. The Arizona Cardinals defense has been at the mercy of a very tough schedule, and it shows in its ratings (28th in EPA/play). While the offense was able to counter its opponents' scores earlier in the year, Arizona's attack is sputtering with the third-lowest points per play average over the last three contests. Dallas is more than happy turning this game into a track meet and thrives on the clean indoor surface at AT&T Stadium. Dak Prescott especially enjoys Jerry's World, with his career metrics spiking at home (103.4 rating at home vs. 92.8 on the road). This is Dallas' first "normal" home game since Week 2 (it played TNF at home in Week 5), and I'm grabbing this Cowboys offense short of the key number of a touchdown. Cardinals vs Cowboys combo Arizona was in a similar shootout spot with the Lions a few weeks back and couldn't keep pace with an explosive offense. Dallas does the same here, pulling away with plenty of points in the second half. CeeDee Lamb is coming off a two-TD day in Week 7 and faces a Cardinals defense allowing the second most touchdowns to rival receivers. Arizona WR Michael Wilson needs to be more involved, and Mike LaFleur knows it. With Arizona playing from behind, plenty of passes come his way, and projections call for as many as 70 yards on Sunday. Our Week 8 expert combo picks have more same-game parlay ideas across the slate. CeeDee Lamb anytime touchdown Michael Wilson 60+ receiving yards Cardinals vs Cowboys touchdown scorer: CeeDee Lamb Lamb looks like the best receiver in the NFL and is coming off a huge performance on Monday, catching two touchdown passes to give him six scores on the season. He will rip through an Arizona secondary ranked among the worst in the land but also featuring plenty of bodies on the injury report in Week 8. The Cardinals run one of the highest rates of zone coverage, and Lamb is excellent at spotting seams in that defense. He's not only a downfield threat but also a catch-and-run weapon, exploiting an Arizona stop unit giving up the seventh most yards after the catch. The Cardinals have allowed 10 touchdowns to WRs (second most), and Lamb's TD forecasts for Week 8 all sit at 60% or higher, with some projections at 80%. For more scorer ideas, see our Week 8 anytime touchdown picks . Cardinals vs Cowboys player prop: Michael Wilson 60+ receiving yards Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur was asked about Michael Wilson's surprising lack of involvement in recent weeks, even with former WR1 Marvin Harrison Jr. traded away. LaFleur danced around the probing question, telling the media, "At receiver, all you can do is control what you can control." Wilson's targets have tanked in the past three games, drawing 22 collective balls for four catches in each of those outings. He's put forth receiving efforts of 30, 32, and 55 yards. He had 13 and 17 targets in the two games prior to that power outage, reeling in 18 receptions for a total of 184 yards. Sunday's trip to Dallas is a pass-positive game script for the large road underdog and while QB Jacoby Brissett has fallen off a cliff, he faces a soft Cowboys secondary making all QBs look like Pro Bowlers (opponent passer rating of 105.2). Brissett is at his best against man coverage and faces a Dallas defense running a higher rate of man-on-man than most secondaries. Wilson rates out as the Cardinals' top one-on-one receiver. Most of his Week 8 projections sit north of 60 yards with a ceiling of 70 yards receiving. Garrett's planned return to practice doesn't mean he'll be ready to play Sunday against the Washington Commanders. But it's a positive sign for his return to the playing field. His return to practice from injured reserve opens a 21-day window for Garrett to be elevated to the active roster or placed on season-ending injured reserve. Micah Parsons will be back at Packers practice this week in a significant step in his return from a torn ACL. Parsons tore his left ACL and damaged his meniscus in Week 15 last season against the Denver Broncos on Dec. 14. His return to the field is taking longer than anticipated. There were reports that Parsons and the Packers were targeting a potential Week 6 return against his former Dallas Cowboys. It's now Week 9. The Packers are off to a 5-3 start without Parsons, which has them in last place in a competitive NFC North behind the 6-1 Vikings and 5-2 Lions and Bears. The Packers are hoping the eventual return of their All-Pro pass rusher can help propel them to the playoffs. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 8 matchup with Minnesota. Christian Booher The Lions have a chance to truly solidify themselves as division title contenders with a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Though the Vikings have underwhelmed offensively at times, they have found a way to start the season 6-0, thanks in part to a dominant defense that will be the best unit Detroit has faced to date. As a result, the pressure will be on Detroit's offense to come up with answers for a group that is led by one of the best defensive minds in football in Vikings coordinator Brian Flores. Jared Goff holds the key, as if he can get the ball out quickly and find answers within the opposition he will have a good chance to lead his group to a dominant performance. It's also an opportunity for the Lions' defense to make a statement against Kyler Murray. I think this game will feature turnovers on both sides, with the unit that gets the ball last ultimately finding a way to win. Detroit gets that advantage, as Goff leads Detroit to a game-winning field goal and a statement division victory. The Lions find a way to win ugly, and remind the league that they are capable of making a playoff run. Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Detroit Lions will face arguably their toughest test of the season yet when they square off with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings Sunday. The Vikings’ defense has been the definition of elite this season, allowing a measly 12.3 points per game (No. 1 in the NFL). You combine that with a stingy pass defense, and Lions signal-caller Jared Goff should have his hands full in the Week 8 affair. Plus, Detroit's defensive back and linebacker groups will need to bring their “A game” against Minnesota pass-catchers Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. It won't be easy for the Lions to emerge victorious in this divisional contest. However, I believe they will on the heels of strong efforts from their pass-rush and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. I believe that Gibbs will help seal the deal for Detroit with several key runs in the fourth quarter, ultimately setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning kick. Lions 24, Vikings 21 John Maakaron This is a game the Lions would ideally like to get out to an early lead, as the Vikings offense is far behind the defense. Brian Flores is sure to bring the pressure from a variety of different spots, but Jared Goff should be able to make good decisions and distribute the football to Detroit’s skill position players. The most interesting matchup may end up being the Vikings offense against Detroit’s defense, given that both units are the clear weaknesses of their respective teams. Expect Jahmyr Gibbs to be responsible for another heavy workload at Ford Field. Lions 23, Vikings 17 Emmett Matasovsky The Lions take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in a headline matchup for Week 8. Overall, I see this being a slightly higher-scoring matchup than last week’s divisional showdown between the Packers and Lions. The Vikings defense is not exactly stout, ranking 23rd in the league in total defense. Combine that with Detroit having a series of unforced errors while breaking Cade Mays into game action at center, and it is hard to see the Lions not outscoring their 20 points last week. Kyler Murray is a mobile quarterback, and that has been a trend of a noticeable struggle for Detroit defenses. That said, the Vikings’ offensive greatness in their first six games also has come against the second-easiest schedule in the league. I see Detroit giving the Vikings the first mark in the latter’s loss column, with Jared Goff making several key plays. picks.headline: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8
picks.blurb: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 4:25 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-0) own the longest active winning streak in the NFL. Dating back to November 30, 2025, they have won 11 games in a row, leaning on an exceptional defense and offense that emphasizes ball control. On Sunday, they head to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions (4-2), who have won two straight and are looking to stay within striking distance of the NFC North lead. The Lions' strengths are the opposite of the Vikings', ranking 2nd in scoring offense and yards per game through seven games, while no one is allowing more yards than Detroit. Minnesota's last four wins have come against teams with a combined record of 7-20. The Lions are the first opponent in a tough four-game stretch where the Vikings will play the Bills , Packers, and 49ers. Skeptics are waiting for Minnesota to come crashing back to Earth, and Sunday could be the first evidence of a regression if the Vikings' offense can't score some points. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings' matchup against the Lions. Kyler Murray will throw for over 300 yards One way you know you're making a bold prediction is if you can visualize people closing out of your article after reading. Minnesota's offense ranks 29th in passing yards. While Kyler Murray has avoided turnovers (two interceptions on 125 attempts), he hasn't consistently attacked defenses downfield. Kevin O'Connell said after last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts that the Vikings' offense is " not far off " from finding its footing. Four runs on the opening drive led to a turnover on downs, and a 3rd-and-5 on Minnesota's second drive ended in an incompletion when RG Will Fries pushed into Murray, who was ready to fire to a wide-open Justin Jefferson. Although the Vikings' defense has been elite since their 11-game winning streak began, O'Connell knows the offense will need to score to keep up with their next four opponents. Expect Murray to be less gunshy on Sunday, but here's hoping that doesn't result in recklessness. Murray goes for over 300, providing optimism moving forward that this passing attack can return to its pre-2025 self. The Vikings will intercept Jared Goff Like Murray, Lions QB Jared Goff has avoided turnovers this year. He has not thrown an interception through six games. However, Goff has still managed to complete 67.3% of his passes for 1,788 yards and 14 touchdowns for an offense that is tied for 4th-best in EPA/play. I'm not sure Minnesota can completely shut down this year's Goff, but they'll pressure him and force him into some bad plays. When the two teams last played, the Vikings forced Goff to turn the ball over five times (two interceptions, three fumbles). It may be difficult to replicate that production, but look for Brian Flores to flummox Goff into at least an extra possession. The Vikings will stop a fourth-down conversion Minnesota was somewhat susceptible to critical conversion attempts last week against Indianapolis. They allowed the Colts to convert 8-of-15 third-down attempts and their lone fourth-down attempt. Detroit converted 5-of-10 third-down attempts against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 but went 0-for-2 on fourth-down, including a controversial 4th-and-1 attempt from their own 24-yard line. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that fear of stopping the Packers' offense and gaining another possession played into last week's decision. I don't see him being nearly that aggressive from his own territory against the staunch Vikings defense. But I do think that this game will be close, forcing Campbell into a tough decision. Give me Flores' unit after they spent a week cleaning things up on the "weighty" downs. This article originally appeared on Vikings Wire: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8

The Minnesota Vikings got some bad news about their starting quarterback on Monday. Coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters Kyler Murray came away from the 19-15 defeat to the Detroit Lions with a hamstring issue. The full extent of his injury isn't yet known. Murray's tenure with the Vikings got off to a rough start in Week 1, as he was forced to exit against the Green Bay Packers in Minnesota's third offensive drive. He attempted to slide while scrambling and took a hard hit from Javon Bullard. Luckily for the Vikings, veteran quarterback Carson Wentz came in and threw for 133 yards and three touchdowns, helping Minnesota come back from a 12-point deficit to win 37-22 and start the season on the right note. Murray is coming off an injury-filled 2025 campaign that saw him play just five games for the Arizona Cardinals as he finished the season with 962 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions. He signed with the Vikings in March and later won the starting quarterback job, hoping to get a fresh start. Unfortunately for him, his season started with an injury, and his performance since returning has been inconsistent. If Murray has to miss time, Wentz will presumably elevate into the starting role for Week 9 matchup with the Buffalo Bills.

away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. home.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell visited Jack Campbell in hospital after neck injury
home.blurb: "Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital," the Lions wrote in a statement posted to social media. "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time." Lions coach Dan Campbell spoke at length about the star linebacker's injury during a news conference on Monday, Nov. 2. The Lions had provided an update about Jack Campbell's status about half an hour before Dan Campbell's press conference was scheduled to begin. Here's the latest on Jack Campbell's status, as well as a way to watch Dan Campbell's Monday press conference where the coach addressed the injury and what the linebacker means to the Lions team. Watch: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell speaks about Jack Campbell What Dan Campbell said about Jack Campbell's injury Dan Campbell did not have a concrete update about Jack Campbell's status but reiterated to reporters the news was "positive" during his news conference. "It's positive," the coach said. "Your prayers are working. Please continue to do that. We'll leave it at that, so continue to pray for him. But it is positive." Dan Campbell also made it clear that he could not provide any additional information about Jack Campbell's condition when asked by reporters. "I can't, so I'm not going to," he said. The Lions coach did make it clear that the team "knows what's going on" and that he has appraised the captains of the situation. He also revealed to reporters he had gotten a chance to visit Jack Campbell and his family in the hospital, along with some other Lions players. "I got to go see him last night," Dan Campbell said. "It was good, it was positive. I got to see his parents, talk to his wife. You know, everybody's in good spirits. It's about the recovery. It's a small setback. That's the family. They're very positive, so that's good in that regard." The Lions coach also was asked exactly what Jack Campbell means to the team as both a player and a person. "I don't even know if I can put it into words," Dan Campbell said, before adding. "He's trustworthy, he's dependable. He'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, all effort. He's just an unbelievable person. Down to earth, very genuine. There's not a man on this team that doesn't respect Jack Campbell and care about him." The Lions have provided few details about Jack Campbell's status since his injury. Their most recent update about his status, before Dan Campbell's press conference, came at 2:31 p.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 2, when they said "preliminary indications are positive" when discussing the linebacker's health. Before that, the Lions most recent update had come at 7:08 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 1, when the team said Campbell was "resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight for continued evaluation and monitoring." home.headline: Detroit Lions signing veteran LB off Patriots practice squad
home.blurb: According to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Detroit Lions are signing veteran linebacker K.J. Britt off of the New England Patriots’ practice squad. The move comes after Detroit suffered two linebacker injuries on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings. Rookie Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury , while Jack Campbell remains in the hospital with a neck injury . No specifics are known at this point about Campbell’s situation, but the team did say that early developments were “positive.” Britt was a fifth-round draft pick for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021, and ended up playing 59 games for them over four seasons—including 15 starts. Last year, he was with the Miami Dolphins, playing in all 17 games and starting one. This year, he failed to make the Patriots’ 53-man roster, but they kept him around on the practice squad, and he was elevated for the team’s Week 5 game against the Raiders. For most of his career, Britt has served as a special teamer. Across just over five seasons in the NFL, Britt has played 1,303 special teams snaps vs. 994 on defense—and he has logged over 250 special teams snaps in four of his first five NFL seasons. There’s a good chance that will be Britt’s role early in Detroit. With the Lions likely to lean more heavily on the likes of Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes, and Trevor Nowaske on defense—with potentially Amen Ogbongbemiga and Joe Bachie mixed in—the Lions will need more experienced depth on special teams and reserves on defense. Britt should be a relatively good fit in Detroit, as a high-effort player who was a captain at Auburn. Detroit should have a good handle on who Britt is as a person and player, as he overlapped with current Lions defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers during his entire time with the Buccaneers.

Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET from MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Jets are 1.5-point favorites on the spread (Jets -1.5; -112), with the over/under set at 46.5. New York is a -125 moneyline favorite while Las Vegas is a +105 underdog. Let's get into my Raiders vs Jets prediction for today's AFC clash. Raiders vs Jets pick: Jets -1.5 (-110) My Raiders vs. Jets best bet is New York to cover the spread (-1.5), with the best price currently available at FanDuel. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Raiders vs Jets Odds Raiders vs Jets Spread : Raiders +1.5 (-108), Jets -1.5 (-112) Raiders vs Jets Moneyline : Raiders +105, Jets -125 Raiders vs Jets Total : 46.5 Raiders vs Jets Preview Raiders Preview This is purely a situational fade of a Raiders team that has "letdown" written all over them. Las Vegas is traveling all the way across the country for an early kick in potential bad weather after an absolutely grueling four-game stretch against the Rams , Bills , Patriots , and Chiefs . The Raiders are bruised, battered, and emotionally drained. The Raiders defense looked great in Weeks 1-2 against Miami and Los Angeles (Chargers), but that was a complete mirage. Since Week 3, the Raiders are basically the worst defense in the NFL across every single major metric. The Raiders also cannot run the football on offense, ranking dead last in both Rush EPA and Rush Success Rate despite investing a first-round draft pick in Ashton Jeanty last year. Without a mobile quarterback to bail them out, this offense is entirely one-dimensional. The Jets are 1-4 in one-possession games and have been a bit unlucky, but the main factor here is that their offense should finally be fully healthy. The Jets have dealt with injuries from the jump, but things are looking up on that front. Getting Dylan Parham back is a huge upgrade at guard, Breece Hall and Braelon Allen are good to go in the backfield, Adonai Mitchell is back to stretch the defense, rookie Omar Cooper looks great, and both tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor are healthy. Geno Smith should finally have a full arsenal to work with in this game, or something close to it. Smith throws short on roughly 55% of his passes, which bodes well in a matchup against a Raiders defense that is the worst in the league against short passing attacks. Yes, the Jets' run defense is problematic (24th in Rush EPA, 25th in Success Rate), and they are dealing with injuries to the defensive line, but as I mentioned above, Las Vegas doesn't have the rushing attack to take advantage of it. Raiders vs Jets Spread Pick to Make This is a terrible travel spot for a bad Raiders team coming off a brutal scheduling gauntlet. The Jets have clear schematic advantages through the air, and their defensive weakness against the run probably won't be exposed by this Las Vegas's running backs. I'll back New York to cover the short number here.
