Neither team is looking too hot at the moment. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak and the Jets just lost to the previously winless Dolphins . To get a feel for how this one could play out, we get the takes from the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. However, playing against a defense that has surrendered the fourth-most points per game and playing at home should give New York's offense a boost. That and the Jets' solid pass defense should keep the Raiders' losing streak going. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 24, Jets 20 The Jets have been the NFL's slowest-starting offense since last season, so this is the week the Raiders finally don't have to dig out of an early hole. Put Kirk Cousins against a defense with one interception in 24 games, and I think the losing streak ends at four. Lamarr Fields -- Raiders 24. Jets 17 The Raiders will have some success running the ball and getting pressure on Geno Smith. Look for Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker to have good games. Levi Damien -- Raiders 20, Jets 19 Nothing about this Raiders team right now inspires confidence in me. And it isn't because they've lost four straight. It's the manner in which they lost them. Either just getting flat out streamrolled or giving up a ton of points and then trying to make a comeback when it's too late. The offensive line is starting to look like who we thought they were and the defense simply doesn't look smart. And playing on the east coast? Ugh. That being said, I have less confidence in Geno Smith. Perhaps that comes from the experience with him in Las Vegas last season, who knows. But I think the Jets record reflects that he's not the answer, with their only wins coming over a hapless Titans team and a low-scoring affair against the Browns. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. away.headline: Las Vegas Raiders Returner Calls His Shot, Ends 15-Year Drought
away.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders had gone 15 years without a kickoff return touchdown. Dylan Laube ended that stretch Sunday at MetLife Stadium, taking a kickoff 95 yards for a score in a 38-33 win over the New York Jets that stopped Las Vegas’ four-game losing streak. Laube, a Las Vegas Raiders running back and the team’s primary kickoff returner, gave the Raiders (4-4) a 14-13 second-quarter lead with the runback. It was the franchise’s first kickoff return score since Jacoby Ford’s 101-yard touchdown against Cleveland on Oct. 16, 2011. It also was the NFL’s first kickoff-return touchdown of the 2026 season. Locked On Raiders host Qiant Myers said Laube had looked close to breaking a return all season. Laube had made the same prediction after being named a Week 8 captain, telling Myers before the game, “I think it could be coming this week.” He credited the return unit for putting him in position, saying the front 10 was “one of the best in the league” and that his job was to hit the opening. Las Vegas still has a larger defensive issue to address before its Week 9 trip to the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 8. But Laube’s return changed the complexion of the Jets game, gave the Raiders a rare special teams breakthrough and supplied a needed contribution from a player who has become one of their most reliable return options. The play carried extra weight after Las Vegas struggled to create separation in a game that became a shootout. The Jets gained 439 total yards, including 166 on the ground, and held a nine-point halftime lead. Laube’s touchdown gave the Raiders an explosive score without asking the offense to put together another long drive. Some or all of this content may have been generated by AI. away.headline: New York Jets Rule Out T'Vondre Sweat for Las Vegas Raiders Game, List David Bailey as Doubtful
away.blurb: Officially ruled out are massive defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat and edge Joseph Ossai. On the cusp of being officially declared out is edge David Bailey, who has missed all three practices this week with a groin injury. He is listed as doubtful on the injury report, and his absence would be a big blow to any Jets hopes of taking down the Raiders. Linemen Darrell Jackson Jr., Nate Lynn and Harrison Phillips will be asked to step into the breach on defense for the Jets. Lynn had a sack against Miami (his first, along with his first NFL tackle), while Jackson has done well in limited appearances. Phillips, who has played for the Vikings and the Bills, has been less successful. His PFF grade is an abysmal 49.2, ranking 102 out of 126 qualified linemen. But he is a big body and will have to step up in the absence of Sweat, who has been a rock in the middle for the Jets. Listed as questionable is running back Breece Hall, who has been out since Week 3 with a quad injury. He was limited during this week’s practices. “He’s a key cog of what we’re doing,” head coach Aaron Glenn said of Hall. “And each time he goes out [and practices], man, there are certain points that he has to hit to make sure that we’re all good and we want to make sure we hit those points.” If Hall plays – a game-time decision – he will likely see limited action and share the backfield with Allen, who has been the No. 2 rusher in the NFL for the time period he’s taken over from Hall as the lead back. Left guard Dylan Parham was given a surprisingly good injury update. He fully participated in practice on Friday and will likely see at least spot duty. He’s been out with a knee injury since Week 3 against Detroit, but was playing as well as any Jets lineman when he went down. The New York Jets will be severely depleted on the defensive line for their Sunday game against the Las Vegas Raiders. The injury news on the other side of the ball is a bit brighter for the Jets. Running back Braelon Allen has been cleared after fully practicing on Thursday and Friday. Allen had a minor ankle injury sustained in the Miami game. The Raiders have a much better health situation than the Jets. The only definite scratch was edge Patrick Johnson. Tight end Brock Bowers practiced fully this week, a big plus for the Raiders, who often use two tight ends.

picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns Prediction: Why Pittsburgh Gets Revenge for Week 4 Loss at Home - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Jobe Morrison Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers get their shot at revenge Sunday when the Cleveland Browns come to town for a Week 8 AFC North rematch . Cleveland beat Pittsburgh in Week 4 by taking advantage of a soft zone defense and an offense that had not yet found its footing. A lot has changed since then. The Steelers' offense has settled in, the defense has mixed up its looks, and Pittsburgh has a clear edge on the ground against a Browns defense that has struggled to stop the run. Here is why the Steelers will even the season series at home. Prediction: Steelers Win 23-16 Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) runs after catch against the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Acrisure Stadium.Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images When the Steelers played the Browns in Week 4, the offense was coming off its first big performance of the season, against the Bengals in Week 3. It still hadn't found its groove. Seven games in, the offense looks much better than it did early in the season, and three games after the loss to Cleveland, it's no longer fair to say it hasn't found its rhythm. Pittsburgh also has an advantage in the run game against this Browns defense . Cleveland has struggled to stop the run consistently, and it allowed three rushing touchdowns and more than 100 rushing yards to the Titans last week. The only concern for Pittsburgh is the passing game. It has produced for most of the season, but it hasn't been as consistent as the Steelers want. Can it take a step forward in this divisional grudge match at home? Sep 18, 2023; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) is sacked by Pittsburgh Steelers safety Elijah Riley (37) during the fourth quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Pittsburgh won 26-22. Credit: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports Let's be honest: The Steelers should have held the Browns to far fewer points in Week 4. To Cleveland's credit, it took advantage of the Steelers' soft zone plan, missed tackles and miscommunications. Since then, the Steelers have mixed up their looks and have graded out as a strong defense by the analytics. There's no excuse for them not to play at a high level at home Sunday. It will be up to the defense to play tighter coverage, make sound tackles and pressure the quarterback. The Steelers have done all three well this season. If they do them again Sunday, they will have a good chance to win. home.headline: Steelers reportedly linked to star WR ahead of NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: The biggest issue for the Steelers’ receiver room, though, is injuries. Three receivers sit on the injured reserve list: Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Cole Burgess. Ben Skowronek is also out with a calf strain right now. That leaves Metcalf and standout rookie Germie Bernard as the top receivers on the team right now. The Steelers have also utilized top running back Jaylen Warren as a receiver this season as he has posted the second most receiving yards (294). The Pittsburgh Steelers might be interested in acquiring a wide receiver in a trade ahead of the NFL deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The team’s top receiver, DK Metcalf, isn’t producing like they’d hoped so far this season. Through eight games, Metcalf has caught 33 of 65 passes thrown to him for 378 yards and one touchdown. Understandably, the Steelers are now reportedly interested in getting a new wide receiver for quarterback Aaron Rodgers , and one name that’s popped up this week is New York Jets star Garrett Wilson, NFL insider Jason La Canfora floated the idea on Monday . Last week, Wilson told reporters that he doesn’t want to request a trade from the Jets, but that he’s aware of how the NFL’s business runs. He will definitely be an expensive get for whichever team decides to make an offer. Wilson, who was the 2022 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, is in his fifth season in New York. He’s shined with the Jets, but the team has still failed to make the playoffs dating back to the 2010 season. He might want to join a team that has postseason potential. And, he would likely be a long-term solution for the Steelers’ offensive goals. The receiver has experience playing with Rodgers when he was on the Jets in 2024 (he played one snap in ’23). Wilson put up his best stats with Rodgers in ’24 as he caught 101 passes for 1,104 yards and seven touchdowns that season. Maybe the partnership needs to reunite in Pittsburgh. Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications. The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Scott Kennedy (3-4) This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina. The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support. This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year. However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense. Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player. The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air. Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16 Gerald Thomas, III (3-4) Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception. There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator. Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers. A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success. Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-4) 99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years. That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500. I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league. I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary. Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 Darius Hayes (3-4) I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field. Atlanta cannot afford to get away from what worked against San Francisco. Establishing the run will help take pressure off Penix while creating opportunities for the offense to control the game. Defensively, the Falcons need to make enough key stops and force the Buccaneers into difficult situations. Tampa Bay is capable of making plays offensively, but Atlanta has shown improvements on that side of the ball. Coming off last week’s momentum-building victory over the 49ers, I like the Falcons to carry that confidence into Tampa. It won’t be easy, but Atlanta does enough on both sides of the ball to earn a hard-fought divisional victory, take over first place in the NFC South, and leave Tampa Bay with a win. Prediction: Falcons 24, Buccaneers 17 Garrett Chapman (3-4) The Falcons are fresh off their biggest win of the season, but they have to take the show on the road on Sunday. They've had a lot of success in Tampa over the last few years, and this team will enter with a lot of confidence with how Michael Penix has been playing. This will be a tight game that I expect will come down to the final drive. The Buccaneer defense is solid, and it will be a difficult test on the road for an offense that hasn't shown it can consistently be a steady unit. Atlanta has a chance to take over the top spot in the NFC South on Sunday, but it won't happen just yet. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice. It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. River Wells, Editor: Falcons 24, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air. I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James. Consensus: Falcons 3, Bucs 2 This is among the closest prediction slates we've had all year. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year. away.blurb: Ex-Falcons WR Signs With 49ers After Injuries - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 183 men's hoops games today Ex-Falcons WR Signs With 49ers After Injuries ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 16: KhaDarel Hodge #4 of the Atlanta Falcons warms up prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) Getty Billy Heyen Tue, November 3, 2026 at 12:21 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Atlanta Falcons will potentially have to watch one of their reliable former players contribute to the San Francisco 49ers in the weeks ahead. The 49ers are injury-battered at the wide receiver position, and they found a former Atlanta wideout who can help their cause. The news emerged Monday that the 49ers have signed KhaDarel Hodge. Why 49ers Signed KhaDarel Hodge The 49ers simply needed some more wide receiver depth right now. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel have both been dealing with injuries, which has really hurt the WR depth chart in San Francisco. The 49ers already have WRs Demarcus Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling on Injured Reserve. That's not to mention Brandon Aiyuk, who remains away from the 49ers with no clear sign of what might happen next in his career. Hodge is a useful enough receiver, but he's more known these days for his special teams prowess. He's on the 49ers' practice squad for right now, but he did appear in three games earlier this season for San Francisco, so they're familiar with him and have him back in the fold. Hodge first joined the Falcons for the 2022 season and played 63 games in Atlanta over four seasons. He caught 13 passes in 2022, 14 passes in 2023, seven passes in 2024 and three passes in 2025. Hodge made the Pro Bowl in 2024 for his play on special teams. Across his four seasons with the Falcons, he had 29 tackles and recovered three fumbles. The Falcons chose not to bring back Hodge for this season, and he latched on with the 49ers, who have played him three games this season (with one catch for 18 yards as well as five tackles). Hodge had previously played for the Rams, Browns and Lions. Now 31, Hodge has made an incredible tenure in the NFL for himself after playing his college football at Alcorn State, Hinds Community College and Prarie View A&M. He went undrafted, but he has now played 121 games and counting. Hodge ended last season with an injury, which might be part of why the Falcons let him go in the offseason. The 49ers signed him in August, waived him at the end of the month, brought him back to the practice squad, elevated Hodge for those three games, and then released him on Oct. 1. Hodge spent October not on a roster, but now he's back with the 49ers to begin November. away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. home.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. It’ll come down to who executes better and the Buccaneers have a golden opportunity to make a statement in a game that could have massive implications for the NFC South race. 4 key matchups to watch as Buccaneers face the Falcons in Week 8 5 Buccaneers who need to thrive in Week 8 vs. Falcons Panthers’ loss to Packers just gave the Buccaneers a golden opportunity in NFC South Todd Bowles had the perfect message for the Buccaneers after blowout win over Panthers Buccaneers down several key players as latest injury report paints ugly picture This article was originally published on thepewterplank.com as Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of We

The Jaguars are set to host the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium in Week 8, with the Jaguars fresh off a bye and also playing at home for the first time since Week 3. With the Colts in complete teardown and rebuild mode, the Jaguars are clearly expected to roll past them this week, something head coach Liam Coen knows he has to be guarded against. "It's innate as a coach. I've been a part of it so many times, especially as an assistant where you're so hyper-focused on your group, like, ‘Hey, I hope my group plays well today. I hope my position plays well today.’ As a head coach in general, I hope we all play well, but I kind of expect us to. I do," Coen said Friday. "I don't expect us to walk out on the field and give lack of effort or guys not run to the football. And is it going to happen on some plays? Yeah. But as a whole, as a group, I do expect these guys to walk out on the field on Sunday and give their best effort for the most part. And is it always perfect? No. And that's what you're striving for, that perfect balance, but it's such an imperfect game. It is nice to know, this is the way I feel, that our guys are going to play on Sundays.” So, how does the national NFL media see the Jaguars and Colts matchup playing Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Seth Walder: Jaguars Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis The Jaguars get a clean sweep here: 22 votes to 0. This isn't the first time the Jaguars have gotten this kind of vote, and it is worth noting that they have been able to prove the voters right each time they are seen as the big favorites, sans a close win against the Philadelphia Eagles. When the votes have been closer, such as in Week 2 and in Week 6, is when the Jaguars have found more trouble but that was never going to be the case here. I think the Colts are going to play hard. I think Shane Steichen is a solid coach. But I just think the Colts were a team that was already lacking the firepower to stack up with the Jaguars before it lost some of its best players. I ultimately expect an MVP-level performance from Trevor Lawrence, who matches up well against the Colts' defensive scheme and tendencies, and I also expect Daniel Jones to have a rough outing. Charlie Disturco Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:26 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts (2-5) and Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) will meet in Week 8 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Florida. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Jaguars are 10.5-point favorites over the Colts on the spread, with the total set at over/under 46.5 points. Jacksonville is a -520 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Indianapolis is a +400 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Colts vs Jaguars prediction and player prop pick for today's game. Colts vs Jaguars pick: Bhayshul Tuten Over 64.5 Rushing Yards (-111) My Jaguars vs. Colts best bet is Bhayshul Tuten to record over 64.5 rushing yards. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Colts vs Jaguars NFL Odds Colts vs Jaguars Spread : Colts +10.5 (-122), Jaguars -10.5 (+100) Colts vs Jaguars Total : over/under 45.5 (-106o / -114u) Colts vs Jaguars Moneyline : Colts +400, Jaguars -520 Colts vs Jaguars Preview for NFL Week 8 Indianapolis Colts Preview: Everything for Sale The fire sale is officially on in Indianapolis. Following a third consecutive loss, the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson ( Seahawks ) and DeForest Buckner ( 49ers ). Josh Downs has also requested a trade, while all eyes have shifted toward the team's prized possession: superstar running back Jonathan Taylor . For now, there are no expected changes at quarterback. Colts head coach Shane Steichen doubled down on Daniel Jones , who threw for just 108 yards last week. The veteran quarterback has struggled mightily this season, throwing more interceptions (7) than touchdowns (4) while posting a career-low completion rate of 59.6%. There is some positive news for Indianapolis, however. Tyler Warren is expected to return to the starting lineup after missing two games with a groin injury. The same goes for Sauce Gardner , while Downs will also suit up despite his trade request. Warren's presence is a must for a Colts receiving room that includes 34-year-old Keenan Allen and journeyman Laquon Treadwell . The question remains: Can the Colts weather the storm and put up a fight against their division rival? The biggest question is how the offensive line will hold up against a formidable Jaguars defense. Indianapolis ranks around league average in rushing yards per game, but those numbers came with Nelson anchoring the offensive line. Taylor is already averaging a career-low 4.2 yards per carry, and losing another key piece up front certainly won't help. The Colts defense has its own issues, ranking in the bottom 10 in points allowed per game and 11th in rushing yards allowed (124.4). Rush defense is definitely Indy's Achilles' heel on the defensive end, ranking 29th in rushing EPA allowed. The pass defense, however, has been surprisingly solid. Indianapolis hasn't allowed a wide receiver room to reach 100 receiving yards since Week 4, while opposing receivers are averaging just 10 receptions per game. Jacksonville Jaguars Preview: Bhayshul Tuten Due for Breakout Game It was a much-needed bye week for the Jaguars, who are coming off two London games filled with late-game theatrics. Jacksonville's defense has been its strong suit this season. Outside of the Texans (34 points), no team has scored more than 17 against this talented unit. The Jaguars rank No. 1 in rushing yards allowed per game (72.2) but have struggled mightily against the pass, ranking 30th while surrendering 274 yards per game. Ultimately, Jacksonville's success will hinge on Trevor Lawrence and the offense finding another gear. The Jaguars are around league average in total offensive production and have maintained a near 50-50 split between the passing and running games. I'd be surprised if Jacksonville's ground game doesn't start to take off soon as Bhayshul Tuten is on the verge of a breakout. The explosive running back possesses elite speed and has already shown the ability to rip off chunk plays. Unfortunately, several of those big gains have been wiped away by holding penalties. Still, Tuten has rushed for at least 65 yards in five of his six games this season. I've been waiting for this offense to take the next step, and there are plenty of weapons to make it happen. Outside of Tuten, Jacksonville has a talented receiving corps led by Parker Washington . We also saw Travis Hunter become more involved offensively before the bye, recording four catches for 59 yards and a touchdown. That increased usage is a trend I expect to continue in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr. has also been the subject of trade speculation ahead of the upcoming deadline. He was benched for the second half against Houston and hasn't recorded a catch in either of Jacksonville's last two games, making his involvement worth watching. One situation worth monitoring is Jakobi Meyers , who enters Sunday questionable after missing Friday's practice with hamstring and ankle injuries. Thomas would likely be relied on to step up in his absence. Another development I've highlighted previously is Jacksonville's increased use of two-tight-end sets. Brenton Strange has been nothing short of excellent, but the emergence of Nate Boerkircher could be just as important moving forward. The second-round pick played a career-high 55% of the snaps before the bye, and I expect his workload to consistently settle in the 50–60% range. Colts vs Jaguars Picks, Betting Analysis I hinted at it earlier, but I expect the Jaguars' ground game to take off. To me, it's a matter of when, not if. Tuten is PFF's No. 1-ranked running back and ranks among the league's best in yards after contact per carry. He draws a Colts run defense that has struggled all season and will be without one of its most important defensive players in Buckner. With Jacksonville entering this matchup as a double-digit favorite, I expect the Jaguars to control possession and lean heavily on the ground game. That should mean a healthy workload for Tuten. Coming off a bye, Tuten should be fresh and ready to take advantage of a spiraling Colts squad. Don't be surprised if he finally breaks the 100-yard rushing mark in this one. home.headline: Jacksonville Jaguars: Get devastating news on standout DT
home.blurb: The Jacksonville Jaguars blew out the Indianapolis Colts 42-7 on Sunday and are now 5-2 on the season. Unfortunately, the Jaguars couldn’t finish the game unscathed, as multiple players left with injuries. Standout defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton suffered an apparent knee injury during the second quarter and was carted off the field. During the postgame press conference, Liam Coen hinted that Hamilton suffered a significant injury as he reflected on his impact on the defense. “When he’s out there laying down and he’s reassuring me. That’s who he is. He’s reassuring me, and has a smile on his face, actually. He trusts God. He trusts himself. He trusts life. He’s just one of those types of people. Tough to see that, obviously.” “There’s not many better humans, better competitors, team guys,” Coen said, via Michael DiRocco of ESPN . “You should have saw D-Ham this week in practice. His leadership [with the] defensive line, individual periods this week, just the human, the competitor. I can’t say enough about him. The Jacksonville Jaguars get devastating news on standout DT According to Ian Rapoport, DaVon Hamilton suffered a torn quad and is expected to miss the rest of the season. This is devastating news for the Jaguars, especially since he’s a strong force behind the league’s top-ranked run defense . Hamilton (likely) finishes with 16 tackles, 13 stops , six pressures, a half sack, one forced fumble, and a fumble recovery across seven games. On top of that, the former third-round pick will become an unrestricted free agent in March, unless something happens contractually. Ruke Orhorhoro , Matt Dickerson , and third-round pick Albert Regis could take on expanded roles alongside starter Arik Armstead . Meanwhile, the Jaguars could be in the market for an interior defensive lineman ahead of next Tuesday’s NFL Trade Deadline. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. The Rams are 3-4 and looking to get back to .500, while the Chargers are still searching for their first win. To preview this game, we caught up with Chargers Wire's Gavino Borquez and asked him five questions about the team, including a final score prediction. What on earth has happened to Justin Herbert and this offense? What's gone so wrong with Mike McDaniel as the OC? Chargers Wire: The Chargers sit at 0-6 and rank dead last in the NFL in points per game (15.0) and EPA per play (-0.190). Herbert is playing the worst football of his seven seasons in the league. He has thrown 5 touchdowns and thrown 8 interceptions, tying for the league high, and has taken 21 sacks. The issues are layered. The offensive line and wide receiver group have been ravaged by injuries. Pre-snap penalties have hindered the unit. And the marriage between Herbert and McDaniel's scheme has not clicked. The two spent roughly four hours in film sessions during the bye week working on mutual accountability and finding spots to build on. We will see if it comes together on Sunday. Are there any key players the Chargers are getting back from injury this week coming off the bye? Chargers Wire: Right tackle Joe Alt is officially cleared and returning to the lineup after missing time with a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has been a full participant in practice coming out of the bye, though still navigating final clearance from a concussion, and is expected to play. Who's an underrated player on defense that the Rams should know about? Chargers Wire: While the average casual fan might not know his name, defensive tackle Teair Tart is widely respected by offensive linemen as a player they need to account for. Tart is known for his run defense prowess, but he has flashed effectively in generating interior pressure. Do the Chargers have any playmakers who can threaten the Rams defense besides Ladd McConkey? Chargers Wire: The Chargers don't possess an alpha weapon, but second-year Tre' Harris has flashed potential as a reliable deep threat . In 5 games, he has caught 15 passes on 26 targets for 225 yards, averaging an efficient 15.0 yards per reception. Though his momentum was temporarily paused by an injury suffered in Week 5 that forced him to miss the Week 6 game against the Chiefs, Harris is trending towards on Sunday. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Chargers Wire: While the Chargers benefit from the return of key offensive pieces in Joe Alt and Ladd McConkey, their vulnerability lies right up the middle. The Bolts' struggling interior offensive line is poised to be the Achilles' heel in this game, allowing the Rams' defensive front to consistently collapse the pocket and get to Justin Herbert. Furthermore, even with the Chargers coming off a bye week, it's hard to tell whether they've made any meaningful offensive changes. Expect the Rams to exploit the center of the line and for their balanced offense to score three touchdowns to secure the victory. Rams 24, Chargers 16. home.headline: Myles Garrett returning to Rams practice, but it's unclear when he'll play
home.blurb: The Rams will open the 21-day window for Garrett to return to the roster, but McVay said the Rams would proceed cautiously before determining when Garrett will play in a game. McVay said there was “a good chance” tight end Terrance Ferguson will return to practice this week but a decision has not been made. Ferguson has been on injured reserve since Oct. 2 because of an ankle injury. With the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10, McVay reiterated that the Rams are counting on the return of Garrett, Ferguson and other key players such as receiver Davante Adams and defensive lineman Kobie Turner as opposed to making deals for new players. Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett , who has been on injured reserve since undergoing knee surgery after the season opener, will practice this week, coach Sean McVay said Monday. The Rams (4-4) play the Washington Commanders (2-4-1) on Sunday in Landover, Md. “I want to be careful to even set any sort of expectations,” McVay said during a videoconference with reporters. “I think just taking it a day at a time is going to be the best way that we can approach it. “Think that’s the right thing for him and really just to see how he responds.” The Rams acquired Garrett in June by sending edge rusher Jared Verse, a first-round draft pick and future picks to the Cleveland Browns for the two-time NFL defensive player of the year, who amassed an NFL season-record 23 sacks last season. Garrett, 30, was sidelined for most of training camp because of a left knee problem. The five-time All-Pro practiced the week before the Sept. 11 opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, but he did not make a tackle in the 27-7 defeat. Garrett said afterward that it was “the worst version of myself,” and that there were times he was thinking about his health rather than what the 49ers were doing on offense. “Getting him back on the field I think is going to be really good overall for the team and as a defense,” cornerback Trent McDuffie said Monday, adding that Garrett’s energy will bolster a unit that is beginning to ascend. McDuffie, who was sidelined against the Arizona Cardinals and the Las Vegas Raiders, intercepted a pass during Sunday’s 24-9 victory over the Chargers before he suffered a back injury that forced him to leave the game. Cornerback Jaylen Watson also left because of a shoulder injury. McVay said both would be evaluated throughout the week before making a determination about their availability for Sunday. Quarterback Matthew Stafford reportedly left the locker room Sunday with an ice pack on his right elbow. McVay said Stafford has “had some soreness there” but said Stafford was better equipped to address the problem. Stafford is scheduled to speak with reporters Wednesday. ... Linebacker Grant Stuard suffered a hamstring injury during warmups before the game against the Chargers, and running back Dean Connors suffered a broken hand during the game and was scheduled to have surgery Monday, McVay said. Additionally, Awosika, Thompson, and Leonard did not practice all week so head coach Jim Harbaugh and the coaching staff knew that they would be without those three players as well, which like James should not have affected the game plan too much. Lastly, for Mack to be available is not a surprise at all, as he was simply resting, and as a veteran, that is fairly normal for Mack so he should be a full go against the Rams' offensive line on Sunday. So, when the game starts on Sunday, it will be interesting to see if the Chargers can come out and have a full 60-minute performance to earn their first win of the year or if the Chargers' struggles will continue and lead to a Rams win as well as the Chargers falling to 0-7. WR Brenen Thompson (quadricep/hamstring) Focusing on James, he was actually placed on IR on Saturday, according to Adam Schefter , which is not really a surprise when considering that it was viewed as a possibility earlier in the week . As a result of that, the Chargers will now officially be without James for at least the next four games, which adds to the fact that James has not played since Week 3. So, the Chargers will need their safety room to step up with James being placed on IR. Now, looking at the big picture for Sunday, the Chargers knew they were more likely than not going to be without James, which should not affect their game plan too much on defense. In the secondary, it is going to be interesting to see if Jackson and Shelly are going to be able to play because the Rams have a great receiver in the form of Puka Nacua, who can take advantage if the secondary is not ready to play. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Denver seems to be finding its stride just a little bit, although a win over the Arizona Cardinals won't convince anyone that the reigning division champions are all the way back. The winner of Sunday's tilt could generate some serious momentum in the AFC West race as the season approaches its midpoint. What gives in the afternoon window of play? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 8 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: For the second week in a row, I'm expecting a low-scoring game. This time, however, I think the Chiefs will find the end zone. Kansas City just needs enough from Rashee Rice and his fellow pass catchers to allow Kenneth Walker to have opportunities similar to the ones he took advantage of in Week 1. The final inactives list will be massive for both teams, but I expect the Chiefs to escape Denver with a narrow win. Jordan Foote: Getting wideout Rashee Rice back in the fold for this one is huge. Given that Xavier Worthy's come back down to earth, Travis Kelce is banged up and Kenneth Walker III has finally looked human, having a formidable weapon on offense is paramount. On the other side of the ball, missing cornerback Mansoor Delane will hurt, but being minus L'Jarius Sneed might just be an addition-by-subtraction scenario. Expect a one-score game that is far from the prettiest, albeit with Kansas City still doing enough to complete the sweep of Denver and maintain first place in the AFC West. Joshua Schulman: The Chiefs are reeling after an ugly loss to Seattle in prime time last week. It’s difficult to imagine the offense looking any more inept than it did a week ago when it mustered just one field goal all night. The Broncos’ defense isn’t quite as dominant as Seattle’s but still is a formidable unit. With that said, we saw who the better team was when these two sides met in Week 1. Denver has been winning in spite of Bo Nix’s play, not because of it, and the KC coaching staff has to have stressed the importance of a game in which it could lose the first-place lead in the AFC West. Tyler Brown: This feels like a tighter game than Week 1, but the Chiefs' strengths match up well against those of the Broncos. Denver will be desperate with the divisional stakes swinging so heavily. With Jonathan Cooper lined up opposite Nik Bonitto, the Broncos have a better edge-rush pairing than they did in September, which puts the Chiefs’ tackle situation under real stress if it ends up in too many obvious dropback situations. The Broncos may perform better this go-around, but the matchup tilts toward the Chiefs. Denver’s rushing defense ranks 28th and leads the league in missed tackles, which is exactly the situation Kenneth Walker thrives in. Getting Rashee Rice back is a bigger deal than it may sound, because it gives Patrick Mahomes another reliable weapon and it lets Xavier Worthy and the rest of the group settle into their roles. On the other side, Denver is 30th in total offense and 25th in scoring, and Nix has struggled when pressured, especially against the blitz. If Steve Spagnuolo gets creative and some pass rushers outside of George Karlaftis step up, that is another major Chiefs advantage. away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. More news : Jonathan Taylor Trade Talks Heat Up as Colts Change Their Stance Delane, the Chiefs’ sixth overall pick, initially injured his right shoulder during the offseason and aggravated it in the season opener against Denver. After returning to the lineup in Week 3, he suffered another setback during Wednesday’s practice ahead of the rematch with Denver. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. More news : NFL to Review New Allegations Against Packers Star Josh Jacobs More news : Jets Send Clear Message on Garrett Wilson Amid Trade Buzz Losing both players is a tough blow to Kansas City’s secondary, particularly against a division rival that’s found its rhythm over the past few weeks. Delane has become the Chiefs’ primary shutdown corner, while Sneed provides experience and flexibility to move around the defensive backfield. Kristian Fulton and Nohl Williams should likely see expanded roles in the meantime. The timing is also less than ideal considering the Chiefs’ upcoming schedule. The Chiefs also seem to be in the business of improving their offense, and they're in the market for a wide receiver , according to NFL insider James Palmer. "The Kansas City Chiefs, to my understanding, have been working the phones for weeks here trying to get a wide receiver for Patrick Mahomes. Is that Brian Thomas Jr.? Is that Josh Downs? They've been kind of weighing their options. (Chiefs General Manager) Brett Veach has done this before. We'll see if he can do it again before the deadline," Palmer said. home.headline: Broncos injuries: Zach Allen and 3 others cleared to play
home.blurb: Allen went down in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. He was able to walk off the field into the team's blue medical tent, but did not return to the game. Allen finished the game standing on the sideline without his helmet as Denver closed out a win. After the game, Allen was asked about the injury and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good." He was listed as questionable for today's game on Friday's injury report. Allen (and all of the players listed as questionable) are active and set to play against the Chiefs today. Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen ( hamstring ) is active for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL this season, totaling 24 tackles, 19 quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, two pass breakups and one forced fumble through seven games. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. The Broncos ' defensive line rotation this season has been led by Allen ( 343 snaps ), Malcolm Roach ( 283 ), Eyioma Uwazurike ( 272 ) and D.J. Jones ( 220 ). home.blurb: Kelce had been nursing an ankle injury this week, and he was a limited participant in practice on Thursday. The good news is that he was a full participant on Wednesday and Friday, which was good news for his status against the Broncos. Chiefs’ Week 8 injury report vs. Broncos: Is Travis Kelce’s ankle injury something to worry about? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 183 men's hoops games today Malik Brown, ClutchPoints Sun, November 1, 2026 at 4:42 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs were able to take care of business against the Denver Broncos at the beginning of the season, and they'll be looking to do the same thing in Week 8. Things could be a little different this time, as the Chiefs had been dealing with some injuries during the week, one of which happened to be Travis Kelce 's issue. It doesn't seem as if there's anything to worry about regarding Kelce, as he doesn't have an injury designation ahead of the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kelce is still making an impact on the field, and though they lost to the Seattle Seahawks last week, he finished with 44 yards. That's about the amount of yards that he's averaging this season, which isn't bad for him. In their first matchup against the Broncos this season, Kelce finished with 71 yards. The hope is that he can have that same production this time around, especially as they face one of the best defenses in the league. The Chiefs also seem to be in the business of improving their offense, and they're in the market for a wide receiver , according to NFL insider James Palmer. "The Kansas City Chiefs, to my understanding, have been working the phones for weeks here trying to get a wide receiver for Patrick Mahomes. Is that Brian Thomas Jr.? Is that Josh Downs? They've been kind of weighing their options. (Chiefs General Manager) Brett Veach has done this before. We'll see if he can do it again before the deadline," Palmer said. Returning to the lineup was WR Rashee Rice, who missed the past two games with a hamstring injury. Additionally, starting RT Jaylon Moore returned after missing Week 7 with a concussion. Can they make it three wins on the year this week down in South Florida? Historically, playing against the Miami Dolphins on the road has been a tall task for the Patriots. The heat, plus struggles against a team that's either been very good or very bad, hasn't led to the best of results for New England. This year, however, should be a solid victory for the Patriots — despite the conditions. "We have to be conditioned," head coach Mike Vrabel said this week. "I think the better that we play, the more we possess the ball, the fresher we'll stay defensively. Hopefully we get the receivers into a rotation. The backs, we rotate. I don't think that the offensive linemen will necessarily rotate. We may play a couple guys based on who's available. That remains to be seen. The edge guys, we rotate. We try to rotate along the defensive line. We like to have our best players available to help us win." X-Factor: QB Drake Maye Last week against the Chicago Bears, Maye had an excellent day — passing for two touchdowns and running in a third. That was against a Bears defense that's in Super Bowl conversations. Against a Miami defense that has struggled all year, the 24-year-old should have a comfortable day in the pocket, even if some starters at both offensive line and wide receiver aren't playing. Last week, Miami scraped out with its first game of the season against a lowly New York Jets squad. However, I frankly do not see a world where that happens again on Sunday. Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has just 1,057 yards and four touchdowns through the air this season, sitting 25th and 27th in the NFL, respectively. Plus, Miami’s fifth-leading receiver, Ryan Miller, is now on New England’s practice squad. All of that to say, the Dolphins are much better off losing this game — to continue plummeting toward an early draft pick — than they are winning it.
