Mandatory Credit: Jasen Vinlove-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con James McKinney Sun, November 1, 2026 at 12:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Our Miami Dolphins, fresh off their first win of the season over the hated New York Jets, will again face off against a divisional opponent tomorrow afternoon. With that in mind, I asked the following question this past week: What are your predictions, bold or otherwise, for the Miami Dolphins' defense and offense in this coming Sunday's game vs. the New England Patriots? Who do you expect to lead the team in key categories like tackles, tackles for loss, pass breakups, interceptions, defensive touchdowns, etc., on defense, and receiving yards, touchdowns, receptions, rushing production, and first downs, etc., on offense? What are your stat-line projections for our key playmakers this week, and/or who will be the team's MVPs on each side of the ball? Below are some of your takes and predictions for tomorrow's game- DalFinsFan is rightfully curious about this oddity in the schedule that seemingly helps a team from a colder climate that just happens to be the Pats. Curious why this is a late game instead of a 1:00pm ko. dedstrk says make it mistake-free and maybe? We need mistake free football and for the Pats to not take the Dolphins seriously enough for most of the game. Run the ball and continue on with the explosives and running the ball for first downs with Malik and OG. Phinette says the route to victory is keeping the ball out of the Pats' offense's hands. Our best shot at pulling off the upset is by controlling the clock. We need to stick with our ground game and avoid the costly three and outs. On defense we have to avoid being torched by the deep ball. If we can force the Pats to grind it out we have a shot. Phoenix6 has Miami narrowly edging out NE for victory #2. Defense: 1 sack, 1 fumble recovery, 2 interceptions. Rodriguez MVP. Offense: Ollie 89yds, 1 TD. Malik 289yds passing, 49yds rushing, 3 TDs. Douglas MVP. Dolphins 🐬 28, Patriots 27. coluccim believes that bad weather would be our best friend on Sunday. Our pass D is god awful, really. Pray for rain Phins1972 is much more focused on the rookies' development across the roster over the final score. We got our one win, and at this point I'm less concerned with the scoreboard than I am with seeing which players take a step forward and which ones don't. I really wish there were a young edge rusher on the roster who looked like a legitimate developmental piece. I'm still not a believer in Chop Robinson. He's played better lately, and credit where it's due, but I'm not sold yet. I'm interested to see whether Caleb Douglas can build on his recent performance and make an impact again. It would also be encouraging to see Chris Bell put together a solid outing. On the ground, I'd love to see Ollie top 100 yards once more. If Miami gets one of those hot, humid afternoons, a big back consistently moving the chains could have Patriots defenders gasping for air by the fourth quarter. If they can keep the game reasonably competitive, that'll be a positive. At this stage, player development is every bit as important as the final score, if not more so. Bill Hazlett has the defense doing their job well enough tomorrow to give us the W. Defense holds up. 28-17 Fins! JUK has Miami dropping this one by double digits. The Pats are clearly a stronger roster top to bottom. I think we will need to win the turnover battle to have a chance which has been the pats weakness but if Maye keep things clean they should win. It's likely to be a tough day for Willis if they get ahead too, as their secondary is so much stronger than our receiver room. We need to keep it close and run the ball well to have a chance. I'll say pats by 10 finfanfromsiam points to this team's long-standing issue covering any decent TEs. Does NE have TEs?? Nuff said…… CluelessNFLfan says that reality sets back in with another loss. The Phins come back down to earth this week. Pats 24, Phins 17. Robert Burstein has Miami losing by two TD's. I do think Miami can keep this game a little close until half time, but overall I think D.Maye will have a big game passing and making plays running. I've got Miami losing 13-27. Jptapt is being positive. Molly Polly II sees another upset on the horizon. I'm calling for an upset…why not! Patriots are favored +7.5. Defense tightens up shot group, Ollie beast mode another 100+ yards. Malik playing at home, confident, ready to prove he's the guy who can lead this team. Huge upset, Finz win with seconds left on the clock, 26-24! 🐬🐬 Gusman says it might be close, or Maye might just make the Dolphins' secondary look silly. If Drake Maye plays as he has for the past 4 games he should carve up the Dolphins secondary. Miami should be able to limit the Pats run game. Pats will attempt to shutdown Miamis run game forcing the Dolphins into passing situations. The Pats have a much better secondary than the Phins. Best bet for Miami is to hope Maye is sloppy and throws a couple picks and loses a fumble or two. The Pats are coming off a 10 day break and are not taking a Miami victory for granted. Should be a fairly close entertaining game. Well, the vote is split, with some of us agreeing with Vegas that the Dolphins are clearly set up for another loss, while others are feeling a bit more positive after pulling out the win last weekend against the NY Jets. As always, I want to thank each of you who makes an effort to join our discussions and answer our Phinsider Question Of The Day. Please join us tomorrow for full game coverage and, of course, the live game thread.

away.blurb: He was already listed as limited with an ankle injury, but now he has a knee problem on top of that. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday, “His status is questionable” to play Sunday against the Dolphins. Brady admirer Veronika Rajek bursts out of tiny bikini showing off sideboob But, Brown did drop multiple passes against the Jets and got an onside kick all wrong The 29-year-old did address reporters on Wednesday and insisted he’s still working to return to full strength from the ankle sprain. He claims he is working hard and has felt some of his prior trademark explosion return, but it's a work in progress. Brown said before practice on Wednesday: “None of that stuff matters. It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

home.blurb: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have been ruled out for Sunday's game at Miami. Brown and Henderson were among those listed as questionable on the team's injury report Friday. Brown hurt his knee during Wednesday's practice, after which he was listed with knee and ankle injuries for the first time this season. He did not practice Thursday or Friday. At running back, Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are expected to take most, if not all, of the carries, while Larison contributes primarily on special teams. On Saturday, the Patriots also ruled out backup offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who has been designated to return off injured reserve but not activated to the 53-man roster. Cornerback Carlton Davis (neck) and linebacker Christian Elliss (chest) are still listed as questionable for kickoff, though Davis has indicated he expects to play for the first time in three weeks. Larison did not take a carry, but caught two passes for nine yards. Without Brown and Henderson, the Patriots have lost significant big-play ability and depth on offense. On Friday, New England listed WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable for Week 8. On the one hand, the Patriots haven't ruled out any players as their active roster gets healthier. However, several key contributors remain on injured reserve (WR Mack Hollins, WR Romeo Doubs, LG Aijah Vera-Tucker, RG Mike Onwenu), while Brown's participation decreasing as the practice week wore on was a noteworthy development. While still managing his recovery from a high-ankle sprain, Brown's knee reportedly "flared up" in practice this week, which landed him on Wednesday's injury report as limited. Brown then didn't participate in Thursday or Friday's session, but the 29-year-old still has a chance to play on Sunday. The Pats top wideout has caught just 6-of-16 targets for 75 receiving yards in two games since returning from injury. On Friday, head coach Mike Vrabel had an update on Brown's status. As for the offensive line, the Patriots are managing injuries there, too. Starting RT Morgan Moses continues to play through a foot injury while C/G Ben Brown is pushing to get back into the lineup. Brown started three games at right guard before exiting the Patriots Week 6 win over the Jets with a knee injury. Brown was a full participant in practice this week, suggesting he could return to the starting lineup. Moving over to the defense, the positive injury news is that the Patriots secondary is expected to be whole for the first time since Week 3. Although he's officially questionable, CB Carlton Davis III (neck) is trending toward playing on Sunday after participating in full for all three practices this week. Davis has missed three straight games and four of the last six contests due to his neck injury, while top CB Christian Gonzalez has also missed time with a shoulder injury. "Yeah, I mean, it's everything," Gonzalez said of Davis's return. "CD is a great vet. Somebody that I lean on a lot, able to talk to, pick his mind about certain things. He's seen a lot of balls, so just having him back out there is amazing. Excited to get all of us back." Although the wide receiver situation is in flux, the Patriots roster health is trending in the right direction, with OL Ben Brown and CB Carlton Davis III expected to return this week. The Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts for the season due to a blood clot, putting Tanner McKee in the starting quarterback position for the foreseeable future. The Eagles have been banged up across the board this season, but especially on offense with DeVonta Smith (out in Week 8) and Saquon Barkley both missing time. That’s led to the Eagles ranking in the bottom five in the league in EPA/Play on offense, and it puts them as underdogs in this divisional matchup against the Commanders. Washington lost star receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season in Week 6, but it's coming off a bye and still has a chance to make a play for the top spot in the NFC East. Daniels was dealing with a dislocated elbow, has played in the last two games – and played well – despite making a critical mistake in overtime in a tie against the New York Giants. If the Commanders don’t turn things around sooner rather than later, there’s a good chance Dan Quinn could be coaching for his job. All week long, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections, and much more for this NFC East rivalry matchup. Here’s a compilation of some of our favorites to get you ready for Eagles vs. Commanders on Sunday night. The Commanders' run defense has been bad this season, ranking 31st in opponent rush success rate, meaning the Eagles should be able to run the ball against them. I still think the Eagles have enough skill on offense to compete with a bad Commanders team, so I'm not ready to lay the points on Washington. I'll back the Eagles as underdogs for a second straight week. Philly has struggled a bit against the pass, ranking 28th in passing yards allowed, in the bottom 10 in passing touchdowns allowed and 25th in EPA/Pass. That’s a great sign for Jayden Daniels, who had his best game of the season throwing the ball in Week 6 against San Francisco. The star quarterback threw for 300 yards and completed 72.5 percent of his passes in a close loss in primetime. He had just 164 passing yards against Philly in Week 1, but Daniels has been much more effective since coming back from a dislocated elbow, combining for over 300 passing and rushing yards in back-to-back games. He’s worth a look on Sunday night with so many other star players banged up. Earlier this season, Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert had four catches for 77 yards and two scores in a Week 1 win over Washington. He has not found the end zone since, but the veteran tight end has remained a big part of the offense. Over the last two weeks with McKee at quarterback, Goedert has been targeted 15 times, catching 11 passes for 109 yards. That workload should eventually turn into some scores, and this is a great matchup for the Eagles tight end to make it happen. Through six games, the Commanders have allowed eight receiving scores to the tight end position. Only the Detroit Lions (10) have allowed more. The Week 8 battle of the NFC East basement pits the Philadelphia Eagles against the Washington Commanders (-5.5) on Sunday, Nov. 1. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but this one could go a long way toward defining the second half of the season. Here are my favorite NFL picks for tonight's game, led by the Over. TOP PICK Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with the Cowboys for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completion rate with two TDs in a loss to the 49ers on Oct. 19. With both defenses leaking, there should be plenty of points, and you'll find more totals ideas in our Week 8 Over/Under predictions . Eagles vs Commanders combo There's a lot of big-name firepower missing on both sides, but I see more meat on the bone for these offenses, especially considering that the complementing stop units are both garbage. Washington allowed Dallas Goedert to find the end zone twice in Week 1 and has given up the second most TDs to tight ends heading into Week 8. With the Eagles' receiving corps running thin, Goedert's role spikes on SNF. Rookie WR Antonio Williams is filling the void left by Terry McLaurin , doing plenty of damage out of the slot. That leaves rookie Antonio Williams in a good place, in terms of his work in the offense. His numbers have been good when Daniels is under center, with his worst yardage performances coming when the QB1 was injured. My Eagles vs. Commanders predictions see a Sunday Night Football shootout in spite of the low total on the board. The Week 8 battle of the NFC East basement pits the Philadelphia Eagles against the Washington Commanders (-5.5) on Sunday, Nov. 1. This division has been a mess in the first two months of the schedule, but this one could go a long way toward defining the second half of the season. Here are my favorite NFL picks for tonight's game, led by the Over. TOP PICK Eagles vs Commanders prediction: Over 40.5 If you read my weekly NFL Underdogs column , you'll see I'm taking the points with the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. A big reason why is this underrated offense. Yes, Philadelphia has a backup under center and is potentially missing its top two WRs again. Yet, the Eagles have looked capable with Tanner McKee at the wheel. And with Saquon Barkley back, they went blow-for-blow with the Cowboys for 45 minutes on Monday until running out of ammo in the final frame. The Washington Commanders defense doesn't put up much of a fuss. Washington is a bottom-tier team in several key defensive measurements , including third-down conversions and red-zone defense. Making up for the soft stop unit is an offense that should at least be able to keep its quarterback clean. Philadelphia's once-vaunted pass rush is no more, boasting the fifth-lowest pressure rate , and that means Jayden Daniels has time in the pocket. Daniels is now four weeks returned from his elbow injury, with a bye in Week 7, and is coming off his best performance of the season. He passed for 300 yards and 72.5% completion rate with two TDs in a loss to the 49ers on Oct. 19. With both defenses leaking, there should be plenty of points, and you'll find more totals ideas in our Week 8 Over/Under predictions . Eagles vs Commanders combo There's a lot of big-name firepower missing on both sides, but I see more meat on the bone for these offenses, especially considering that the complementing stop units are both garbage. Washington allowed Dallas Goedert to find the end zone twice in Week 1 and has given up the second most TDs to tight ends heading into Week 8. With the Eagles' receiving corps running thin, Goedert's role spikes on SNF. Rookie WR Antonio Williams is filling the void left by Terry McLaurin , doing plenty of damage out of the slot. He burned the Eagles in his NFL debut and is projected for as many as 46 receiving yards in Week 8. Our Eagles vs. Commanders prop picks and Week 8 expert combo picks have more ways to attack this game. Dallas Goedert anytime touchdown Antonio Williams 30+ receiving yards Eagles vs Commanders touchdown scorer: Dallas Goedert With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks still hurting, tight end Goedert sees a spike in his involvement in the passing game. Goedert drew seven targets for five receptions in Week 7 and has been McKee's safety blanket during his two-game stint as the starter. The Eagles face a Commanders defense that has been bullied by rival tight ends this season. Washington ranks dead last in DVOA vs. tight ends, allowing the seventh most yards to the position along with eight touchdowns to TEs in just six games. Goedert is responsible for two of those touchdowns, with a pair of scores in the win over Washington in Week 1. His touchdown forecasts for this return matchup range from 19% to as high as 44%, with the majority at 30% or higher. See all of our Eagles vs. Commanders touchdown picks for more options. Eagles vs Commanders player prop: Antonio Williams 30+ receiving yards Terry McLaurin's injury has created a vacuum in the Washington pass game, shuffling around the healthy WRs. That's a commodity the Commies are running short on in Week 8. On top of McLaurin's season-ending injury, Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks are both on the injury report for SNF. That leaves rookie Antonio Williams in a good place, in terms of his work in the offense. His numbers have been good when Daniels is under center, with his worst yardage performances coming when the QB1 was injured. Head coach Dan Quinn told the media he was thrilled with Williams' development and Football IQ, following a 50-yard outing in Week 6. Williams has carved out a spot as Washington's top slot option, playing the inside position on almost half his snaps. That matches up well against Philadelphia, which has struggled to contain slot receivers this season. Williams caught all four balls his way for 64 yards and a touchdown in his pro debut versus the Eagles in Week 1. His Week 8 projections all sit north of 30 yards with a ceiling of 46+. My number boils down to 37 yards from the Commanders' first-year receiver. Want more NFL player props? Check out our NFL player prop projections ! home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Bears take their surging offense into Seattle for a matchup with one of the NFL's best defenses Getty Images In the Week 8 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Seattle Seahawks host the Chicago Bears . Seattle enters this game fresh off a victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs , snapping a two-game losing skid. The Seahawks' defense is settling in and once again looks like one of the best units in the league, but faces one of its toughest tests of the season on Monday night. Chicago enters having won both of its games since starting quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury, improving to 5-2 in the process. The Bears have looked like one of the best offenses in the NFL whenever Williams has been on the field, but they, too, face arguably their toughest test of the season on Monday evening. Will Seattle make it back-to-back wins, or will the Bears ruin their evening with a road upset? How to watch Seahawks vs. Bears live Date: Monday, Nov. 2 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lumen Field (Seattle) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -3, O/U 46.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ball Chicago has scored, 59, 31 and 30 points in the three Caleb Williams starts that were not played against the Minnesota Vikings in a driving rainstorm. The Bears piled up 552, 368 and 405 yards in those three games, and turned the ball over only twice in those contests. For the season (including the game against Minnesota), Williams has completed 71% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt, both of which are career-high figures. He has thrown five touchdowns against one interception and rushed 24 times for 128 yards and two additional scores. Williams has generally thrown short passes, with an average depth of throw of only 7.0 yards, according to Tru Media. Despite that, he has created explosive passing plays at the third-highest rate in the league (10.7% of dropbacks). That's thanks in large part to the fact that the Bears are averaging 6.4 yards after catch per completion on his throws, the fourth-best mark in the league. The Seahawks, though, limit YAC as well as just about any team in football. They've allowed only 4.5 yards after catch per completion, which ranks third-best in the NFL. They play shell coverages a lot of the time, and they rally to the ball and tackle as well in the secondary as anybody. Their defensive backs and linebackers rarely miss opportunities to bring ball-carriers to the ground. The Bears generally want to run the ball more often than almost any team in the league, with a 48.7% rush rate, according to Tru Media. The Seahawks are elite at stopping the run, however, as we saw last week against Kenneth Walker III . D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson will have their work cut out for them here, even against a defense that plays a lot of nickel and dime and doesn't load the box. The Chicago offensive line will have to do a lot of work to move Seattle's defensive front off the ball, which has proven extremely difficult for opposing lines this year. When the Seahawks have the ball Seattle's offense is built almost entirely around the exploits of superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba . JSN leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards, 43 receiving first downs and eight receiving touchdowns. He has been targeted on 36.3% of the team's pass attempts, which ranks as the No. 1 mark in the NFL. So does his 33.9% targets-per-route-run rate, which is narrowly ahead of CeeDee Lamb's . Smith-Njigba has more receptions than the next three closest players on the Seahawks: AJ Barner , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed combined for 53. His 867 yards are also considerably more than the 562 that trio has combined as well. They are ancillary pieces at best, and typically they are scarcely involved in the offense. Shaheed is also out on Monday night, which means the secondary options will be even more limited than usual. The Bears, like everyone else in the league, do not have anyone who can cover Smith-Njigba. It's not possible. The best chance to limit him is to get to Sam Darnold and force hurried decisions that lead to turnovers. Darnold, despite missing time due to injury, leads the NFL with eight interceptions. Under pressure, he has been dreadful, completing only 26 of 66 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and four picks. He ranks second-to-last in the league in EPA per dropback on pressured plays, per Tru Media. If the Bears can get into his face, they can force him into mistakes and flip the game on its head. Something that will help them in that effort is the arrival of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who is a game wrecker on the interior. Simmons is among the league leaders in both pressures and sacks when lined up inside. He'll have to deal with what is now one of the best guard duos in the league in Quenton Nelson and Grey Zabel , and Simmons could also see his snaps limited in his first game with his new team. (Nelson is likely to play a full complement in his Seattle debut, given how reluctant teams are to rotate offensive linemen.) The Seattle running game should get a boost from the expected returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price . Charbonnet hasn't played all season after tearing his ACL during last year's Super Bowl run, while Price has been out since Week 3 with a chest injury. The combination of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has largely been ineffective, and even if Charbonnet and Price can generate slightly below-average efficiency, they'll represent an improvement over the incumbent duo. The Bears have given up an average of 4.4 yards per carry this season, which ranks 23rd in the league. Seattle's defense is looking like the unit we expected it to be coming into the year. The Seahawks just shut down Kenneth Walker last week; they should be able to do the same to D'Andre Swift. That puts the entire game on Williams' right shoulder. He can handle that, of course, but it's incredibly difficult to do against Mike Macdonald's unit. That's especially true if the Seahawks get Price and Charbonnet back in the lineup at running back and can run the ball with some degree of success. Pick the Seahawks to take care of business at home.
